about: The root list of the two born tongues: attested Sanskrit words chosen for this world, with the form each takes in the householders' tongue (hearth) and the sand-country tongue (sand). The daughter forms are produced by derive.mjs from rules.json; `node derive.mjs --roots` checks them and `node derive.mjs --roots --fill` rewrites them.

fields.word: The headword in IAST, in the stem form the dictionary gives.
fields.pos: m., f., n. (noun genders), adj., adv., num.
fields.gloss: The sense used here, from the dictionary entry. Only a sense the dictionary cites from a text is given: one it knows only from the old word-lists (marked L. there) is left out. Other senses of the word are not listed, unless `note` gives one.
fields.ref: Where the word is attested: MW is Monier-Williams, A Sanskrit-English Dictionary (1899), by page and column of the printed book. Apte is V. S. Apte, The Practical Sanskrit-English Dictionary (1890), by headword, and is cited where Monier-Williams names no text for the sense.
fields.hearth: The form in the householders' tongue.
fields.sand: The form in the sand-country tongue.
fields.skip: Tongues (hearth, sand, cutters) in which the form is not to be used, each with the reason. A form is skipped because it falls together with another root or because it reads badly.
fields.alone: Tongues (hearth, sand, cutters) in which the word may be used inside a joined name but not as a whole name, with the reason.
fields.note: Another sense of the word that a reader of Sanskrit will hear in it, or a limit on its use. Read it before the root goes into a name.
